description: Principal, rate, time, interest and amount

lessons.title: What is Interest?
lessons.intro: Interest is extra money paid for borrowing or earned for saving. Banks pay you interest when you keep money with them.
explanation: Save money in a bank and it pays you interest.
Borrow money and you pay interest back.
Interest is always extra on top of the original amount.
lessons.rule: Interest is extra money for borrowing or saving.
lessons.tip: Interest is always added on top.

steps.text: Interest is extra earned on it.
steps.tip: You get back more than you put in.

lessons.title: Principal
lessons.intro: The principal is the original amount of money borrowed or saved.
explanation: If you save 1000 rupees, the principal is 1000.
Interest is calculated on the principal.
Principal is where every interest sum begins.
lessons.rule: Principal (P) is the starting amount.
lessons.tip: Find the principal first.

lessons.title: Rate of Interest
lessons.intro: The rate tells how much interest is charged per 100 rupees each year.
explanation: A rate of 5% means 5 rupees per 100 each year.
Higher rate means more interest.
Rate is given as a percent per year.
lessons.rule: Rate (R) is percent of principal per year.
lessons.tip: Read the rate as '% per year'.

lessons.title: Time Period
lessons.intro: Time is how long the money is borrowed or saved, usually in years.
explanation: 2 years means interest builds for 2 years.
Longer time means more total interest.
Keep time in years for the basic formula.
lessons.rule: Time (T) is the number of years.
lessons.tip: Use years unless told otherwise.

lessons.title: Putting the Pieces Together
lessons.intro: Every simple-interest problem needs principal, rate, and time.
explanation: Spot P, R, and T in the question.
Each has its own role in the formula.
Label them before you calculate.
lessons.rule: You need P, R, and T for simple interest.
lessons.tip: Underline P, R, and T as you read.

levels.label: The SI Formula
levels.subtitle: P times R times T over 100

lessons.title: The Simple Interest Formula
lessons.intro: Simple interest uses one neat formula: multiply principal, rate, and time, then divide by 100.
explanation: SI = (P x R x T) / 100.
The 100 comes from the percent.
lessons.rule: SI = (P x R x T) / 100.
lessons.tip: Multiply P, R, T, then divide by 100.

lessons.title: Why Divide by 100?
lessons.intro: The rate is a percent, so we divide by 100 to undo it.
explanation: Dividing by 100 turns percent into a fraction.
That is why the formula has a 100.
lessons.rule: The 100 converts the percent rate.
lessons.tip: Percent always brings a divide-by-100.

lessons.title: Order of Multiplying
lessons.intro: You can multiply P, R, and T in any order.
explanation: P x R x T gives the same answer as T x R x P.
Multiply the easy pair first.
Then divide by 100 at the end.
lessons.rule: Multiplication order does not change the result.
lessons.tip: Pick the easiest order to multiply.

lessons.title: Keeping Units Right
lessons.intro: Use rupees for money and years for time.
explanation: If time is in months, change it to years first.
6 months = half a year = 0.5.
Matching units keeps the answer correct.
lessons.rule: Use years for T in the basic formula.
lessons.tip: Convert months to years before using.

lessons.title: Reading SI Problems
lessons.intro: Find P, R, and T, then plug them in.
explanation: '1500 at 4% for 3 years' gives all three values.
Then apply the formula.
lessons.rule: Identify P, R, T before using the formula.
lessons.tip: Label each number as you read.

lessons.title: Interest for One Year
lessons.intro: Finding interest for a single year is the simplest case.
explanation: SI for 1 year = (P x R)/100.
P 2000, R 5: SI = 100 for one year.
Multiply by more years for longer periods.
lessons.rule: One-year SI = (P x R)/100.
lessons.tip: Leave out T when T is 1.

lessons.title: Interest for Several Years
lessons.intro: For more years, multiply the one-year interest by the number of years.
explanation: One year SI 100, for 3 years: 300.
Simple interest is the same each year.
Multiply by T for the total.
lessons.rule: Total SI = one-year SI x number of years.
lessons.tip: Simple interest stays equal each year.

lessons.title: Bigger Principals
lessons.intro: A larger principal earns more interest at the same rate.
explanation: 5000 at 5% for 1 year gives 250.
Double the principal, double the interest.
Keep dividing by 100 at the end.
lessons.rule: More principal means more interest.
lessons.tip: The rate and time being equal, P decides size.

lessons.title: Higher Rates
lessons.intro: A higher rate earns more interest on the same money.
explanation: The bigger rate gives bigger interest.
Compare rates to compare earnings.
lessons.rule: A higher rate earns more interest.
lessons.tip: More % means more money.

lessons.title: Interest in Stories
lessons.intro: Pick out P, R, and T, then compute the interest.
explanation: '3000 at 5% for 2 years' gives SI 300.
Plug the three values into the formula.
Answer in rupees.
lessons.rule: Identify P, R, T, then apply the formula.
lessons.tip: Underline all three values.

lessons.title: The Amount
lessons.intro: The amount is the total you have at the end: principal plus interest.
explanation: Amount = P + SI.
The amount is always bigger than the principal.
lessons.rule: Amount = Principal + Simple Interest.
lessons.tip: Add the interest back to the principal.

lessons.title: Finding the Amount
lessons.intro: First find the interest, then add it to the principal.
explanation: Compute SI with the formula.
Add SI to P for the amount.
The amount is what you finally get or owe.
lessons.rule: Compute SI, then add P.
lessons.tip: Two steps: interest, then add.

lessons.title: Amount for Savers
lessons.intro: Savers receive the amount when they withdraw.
explanation: Save 2000, earn 200 interest: get 2200.
The bank returns principal plus interest.
More interest means a bigger amount.
lessons.rule: Savers get principal plus interest back.
lessons.tip: Amount is your total payout.

lessons.title: Amount for Borrowers
lessons.intro: Borrowers repay the amount, not just the principal.
explanation: Borrow 1000, interest 150: repay 1150.
The lender wants the interest too.
The amount is the full repayment.
lessons.rule: Borrowers repay principal plus interest.
lessons.tip: Repayment equals the amount.

lessons.title: Amount in Stories
lessons.intro: Find SI, then add it to P to get the amount.
explanation: '2500 at 4% for 2 years': SI 200, amount 2700.
Do the interest step first.
Then add for the amount.
lessons.rule: Amount = P + SI once SI is found.
lessons.tip: Never forget to add the principal.

lessons.title: Putting It Together
lessons.intro: You can now find interest and the final amount for any simple-interest problem.
explanation: Find SI with (P x R x T)/100.
Add SI to P for the amount.
Check your units are rupees and years.
lessons.rule: SI then amount: two reliable steps.
lessons.tip: Compute interest, then add the principal.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Banks
lessons.intro: Higher interest means a better savings deal.
explanation: Bank A 5%, Bank B 6% on the same money.
Bank B earns more interest.
Compare the interest to choose.
lessons.rule: Pick the higher interest for savings.
lessons.tip: More interest is better for a saver.

lessons.title: Longer vs Shorter Time
lessons.intro: More years means more simple interest.
explanation: Same P and R: 3 years earns more than 2.
Interest grows steadily each year.
Time multiplies the yearly interest.
lessons.rule: More years, more interest.
lessons.tip: Each extra year adds the same interest.

lessons.title: Checking Your Work
lessons.intro: A quick check keeps answers sensible.
explanation: Interest should be smaller than the principal for small rates.
Amount must be bigger than the principal.
Re-subtract: amount - P should equal SI.
lessons.rule: Amount - P should equal SI.
lessons.tip: Subtract back to verify.

lessons.title: Simple Interest Master
lessons.intro: Combine every skill to solve full interest problems.
explanation: Read for P, R, and T.
Find the interest, then the amount.
State the answer clearly in rupees.
lessons.rule: Find SI and the amount with confidence.
lessons.tip: Label, compute, and check.
